attributes.residual: ONE NAMED MECHANISM, unchanged at real 18 / 289 insns / multiset IDENTICAL: a first-web register tie-break with a schedule shadow, 5 instructions at 0x424-0x440. Aligned view -- TARGET: lwz r3,gSysFlags / li r0,4 / mtctr r0 / lwz r5,gPadCur / rlwinm r0,r3 / lis r3,gPadStartHoldTimer@ha / stw r0,gSysFlags / li r6,0 / addi r4,r3,@lo. OURS: lwz r4,gSysFlags / li r0,4 / lis r3,@ha / mtctr r0 / rlwinm r0,r4 / stw r0,gSysFlags / addi r4,r3,@lo / lwz r5,gPadCur / li r3,0. Both sides load the flags FIRST, so emission order is NOT the discriminant: the allocator gives r3 to the gPadStartHoldTimer @ha temp in our build and to the gSysFlags temp in the target, and every other difference is downstream of that one choice (target must re-materialise `lis r3` AFTER the rlwinm frees r3, which sinks the address pair below the store and pushes the loop's byte accumulator to r6; ours frees r3 early, hoists the lis above mtctr, and colours the accumulator r3, displacing the loop address temp to r6). The two competing webs have near-identical live ranges (flags 0x41c-0x42c, @ha temp 0x424-0x434), which is why every source-level lever tried so far is inert -- nothing the source can say reorders two same-length webs. NEXT AGENT: do not re-spend declaration, statement-order, alias-spelling or accumulator-form levers. The only untried classes are (a) a lever that lengthens or shortens ONE of the two webs so the tie is not a tie, and (b) the WebFrank path, which is a permutation PLUS recolor and therefore needs the combined permutation+recolor equivalence checker that claim.parked.mbrendertext-color-tiebreak.20260831.v3 already showed does not exist.
